messages:
morgan: Quick note — during the quantized bring-up of redwood-mini-13B-int4 I hit a reproducible divergence when using long prefixes (>32k tokens). Not full crash, but outputs start drifting ~500 tokens after a long prefix.

Priya: uh oh. repro script?

morgan: Minimal repro attached below. Happens both on Dedicated and locally with the same quant profile. Steps: 1) prefix with 35k tokens (synthetic repeating paragraph) 2) prompt question, sample temp=0.2 3) compare tokens vs float32 baseline.

alex_k: can you paste the prompt/outputs? even a short diff helps.

morgan: pasted —
```
# prefix = "lorem ipsum..." repeated 1750 times (≈35k tokens)
> prompt: "Summarize the above in two sentences."
-- baseline (float32): "The text describes..."
-- quant int4: "The text shows..." (semantically similar) until token 512 then:
-- quant int4 at token 1024: starts repeating small fragments and occasionally inserts unrelated tokens like "[UNK]"
```

Priya: does kv-cache indexing look off? maybe an off-by-one when wrapping for > 32k window?

morgan: I instrumented the cache indices. Looks like prefill writes at indices up to N, but during generation the lookup treats the rotary-phase offset as if the sequence length = 32k, not 35k. So effective RoPE application is misaligned for the tail.

dana: could be a signed vs unsigned arithmetic bug when computing pos % max_window. Seen that before in a different runtime. Any logs?

morgan: yes, added debug prints around kvcache write/read: 
```
WRITE idx 34987 -> shard0 offset 12587
READ idx 34987 -> shard0 offset 587
```
Mismatch there. On float baseline offsets are identical.

Priya: interesting. Does quantization change memory layout / alignment that could cause a pointer rollover?

alex_k: also try toggling rotary base scaling — maybe quant kernels changed how we compute phase multipliers (float32 math vs int8 lookup).

morgan: ran quick experiments:
- disable int4 fused-rope optimization -> behaves like baseline
- enable fused-rope int4 kernel -> divergence reproduces

morgan: so it's likely the fused/kern path applying RoPE in int4 has a bug when seq_len > configured window and we rely on wrap arithmetic.

eval-bot: perf/eval results queued: 2470001112. Longprefix-diff score: 0.62 -> regression vs float baseline 0.98 (higher is better).

Priya: good find. Next steps: 1) add assert in kvcache read/write that offsets match at prefill time and read-time (fail fast), 2) add a unit test exercising wrap > window, 3) bisect kernel change that introduced fused-rope int4 path.

dana: I'll take the unit test + assertion. alex_k, can you bisect the int4 kernel commits? probably in the recent optimizer PR.

alex_k: yup, starting bisect now. ping me if you need a quick hotfix to disable fused-rope on Dedicated for customers.

morgan: quick workaround I used locally: set "rope_wrap_policy": "no-fused-int4" in runtime config — generation matches baseline but perf drops ~8% so not ideal for production.

deploy-bot: Note: changed runtime flag "rope_wrap_policy" on dedicated-pool-3 to "no-fused-int4" at 2470001140 by alex_k (planned rollback when fix lands).

Priya: thanks. Can we also run a short sweep: int4 vs int8 vs float32 across seq lengths [16k,24k,32k,40k] and collect token-level divergence? I want a small matrix for the postmortem.
morgan: on it. I'll post CSV here when done. For now, disabling fused path on affected customers and adding repro + unit tests.

alex_k: bisect found likely culprit: commit 3f2a9c "fused-rope: inline phase mul for int4". Reverting that commit locally removes divergence. Filing PR to patch arithmetic and add test.

Priya: solid. thanks team. Medium priority incident — label as "regression: longprefix-quant-rope" and include eval CSV when ready. :thumbsup:

morgan: CSV uploaded: https://s3.redwood/repro/2470001111-longprefix-diff.csv

dana: grabbing it now, will add unit test PR in ~2 hours.
